title: Thesys Launches OpenUI 1.0 to Open Source AI Interface Generation
summary:
Interactive visual elements can now be generated by artificial intelligence agents to replace standard text-based chat responses. Thesys has released a toolkit called OpenUI 1.0 that enables AI to write a compact language that renders functioning interfaces on screen in real time. This latest version introduces custom actions, allowing buttons within a generated answer to trigger an application's native code across any model, including open-weight versions running on private hardware.

A Thesys benchmark of 46 interface briefs across six models found that OpenUI used 58% fewer output tokens than Vercel's json-render and 52% fewer than Google's A2UI. The release follows the shift toward 'Intelligent UI' pioneered by ChatGPT, which replaces long paragraphs with interactive charts and tables. The framework's early open-source preview recorded more than 6 million downloads and 10,000 GitHub stars over six months.

selectedTweets.text:
Thesys has released OpenUI 1.0, its open-source framework that lets agents create working interfaces inside apps.

On Thesys' own benchmark of 46 interface briefs across six models, OpenUI used 58% fewer output tokens than Vercel's json-render and 52% fewer than Google's A2UI.

> OpenUI allows models to write a compact UI language that renders on screen while the answer is still being generated.

> It works with any model, including open-weight ones running on a team's own hardware.

> Version 1.0 adds custom actions, allowing buttons inside a generated answer to activate an app's own code.
